_readme: English descriptions for PDOK services and layers. Hand maintained.
This file is separate from resources/layers-pdok.json because that catalogue
is regenerated wholesale and would discard curated translations.
Keys are the exact Dutch source descriptions from the generated catalogue.
Descriptions are translated as English prose; official product names, acronyms,
codes and machine identifiers are preserved where appropriate.
If a key is absent, the plugin safely falls back to the Dutch original.

abstracts.De COROP-gebieden zijn in 1970 vastgeste: The COROP regions were established in 1970 by the Coordination Committee for the Regional Research Programme (COROP). They were developed according to the nodal principle, using commuting flows as the basis. In some places this principle was relaxed so that the regions follow provincial boundaries. When municipal reorganisations cross COROP boundaries, the classification is adjusted. COROP regions are further subdivided into COROP subregions and COROP-plus regions. There are more COROP subregions than COROP regions; the additional areas are Greater Amsterdam, Greater Rotterdam and North-East North Brabant.

abstracts.De Gewaspercelen bestaan uit de locatie: The Crop Parcels dataset contains the locations of agricultural parcels in the Netherlands together with the crop grown on each parcel. The dataset is a selection of information from the Key Register of Parcels (BRP) of the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO). The agricultural parcel boundaries are based on the boundaries in the RVO Reference Register, formerly the AAN dataset (Agricultural Area of the Netherlands). Each year, the parcel user must delineate the crop parcels and indicate which crop is grown on each parcel. A dataset is generated for each year with a reference date of 15 May. View services and a download service are available for the most recent crop parcels. For the years 2009 through 2022, only Atom download services are available.
abstracts.De NUTS, Nomenclature des Unités Territo: NUTS, the Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics, is the regional classification used by Eurostat. It was introduced to provide comparable regions across Europe and thereby make regional European statistics comparable. NUTS has three levels. For the Netherlands these broadly correspond to the following national classifications: NUTS 1: Landsdeel regions; NUTS 2: Provinces; NUTS 3: COROP regions. There is one difference: Dutch national classifications may undergo boundary changes every year, whereas the NUTS classification can normally be changed only once every three to four years. In the intervening period, figures based on the Dutch national classification can therefore differ from figures based on the European NUTS classification. More information about NUTS is available from Eurostat.

abstracts.Deze dataset bevat de naar INSPIRE thema: This dataset contains data on soil borehole investigations harmonised to the INSPIRE theme Soil, originating from soil-oriented boreholes. abstracts.Een milieuhygiënisch bodemonderzoek is e: An environmental soil investigation is an investigation in which the presence of contaminants in the soil within the investigation site is assessed. The soil investigation is generally carried out by third parties, for example under contract to a data owner that is also the project initiator. It may also be submitted by a project initiator other than a government body to the competent authority as part of a statutory procedure, such as a permit procedure or notification. The urban region, understood functionally, consists of a metropolitan agglomeration and the surrounding area containing smaller settlements such as towns, villages and hamlets that are connected to the agglomeration through many types of relationships. These relationships concern daily commuting between home and work, movements of households and businesses, and use of urban facilities. An urban region can therefore be regarded as a combination of a regional labour-market, housing and service area. Two criteria were used to define relationships between a metropolitan agglomeration and its surrounding area: commuting flows based on municipality of residence and work from the Labour Force Survey for the combined reporting years 1995-1997, and movements within and between municipalities from statistics on intra-municipal moves and domestic migration for 1996-1997. For each criterion a non-hierarchical cluster analysis using a symmetric algorithm was performed, after which the results were analysed together. Final delineation of metropolitan agglomerations and urban regions took place in close consultation with the Advisory Committee for Regional Statistics, representing major users of CBS regional data including ministries, municipalities, planning agencies, academia and business. abstracts.Inspire geharmoniseerde dataset van het: INSPIRE-harmonised national Water Framework Directive (WFD) Groundwater Bodies dataset. Under the WFD, a groundwater body is an important unit about which water managers must report. A groundwater body is a coherent mass of groundwater. The Dutch Water Act uses a broader interpretation of the term than, for example, the WFD or the Groundwater Directive. The European directives limit the definition to water below the ground surface in the saturated zone, i.e. all water below the groundwater table. Dutch legislation does not make this distinction: under the Water Act, all water moving freely in the soil is groundwater. The 2009 Water Quality Requirements and Monitoring Decree (Bkmw 2009) does, however, contain the narrower European definition, under which only water in the saturated zone is groundwater. The groundwater objectives of the WFD and Groundwater Directive therefore focus on that water. All groundwater in the Netherlands belongs to a groundwater body. The Netherlands distinguishes 23 groundwater bodies, which are designated and managed by the provinces.

INSPIRE-harmonised national Water Framework Directive (WFD) Surface Water Bodies dataset. Under the WFD, a surface water body is an important unit about which water managers must report. A surface water body is a coherent body of water occurring freely at the Earth's surface, including the substances present in it, the associated bed and banks, and its flora and fauna (source: Environment and Planning Act). The national dataset consists of line features for surface water bodies in the 'River' category and polygon features for the 'Lake', 'Coastal Water' and 'Transitional Water' categories, as well as territorial waters from 1 to 12 nautical miles. Regional surface water bodies are designated and managed by the water authorities, and national waters by Rijkswaterstaat.

abstracts.Natura 2000 is het samenhangend netwerk: Natura 2000 is the coherent network of protected nature areas in the European Union comprising sites designated under the Birds Directive and Habitats Directive. Natura 2000 sites combine both types. When the Nature Conservation Act came into force in 2017, areas previously designated as protected natural monuments under the Nature Conservation Act 1998 lost that designation by operation of law. For Natura 2000 sites overlapping those former protected natural monuments, the objectives associated with the monument designation therefore ceased to apply. There are 162 Natura 2000 sites in total, including four marine sites in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of the North Sea. The current Birds Directive sites were designated between 1995 and 2016. Habitats Directive sites are designated through designation of the relevant Natura 2000 sites. On 19 June 2024, a boundary change for Rijntakken took effect. Boundary changes are incorporated up to the issue date of this dataset. Where no final Natura 2000 designation decision is yet in force, the boundary from the draft decision is used. If no draft decision has been published, the boundary from the European Community List is used; if that list has not yet been updated, the boundary from the nomination for that list is used. See the STATUS attribute for this information. The boundaries apply above ground and in water, except for site parts coded 'HR groeve' in the BESCHERMIN attribute, where only the underground limestone quarries form part of the Habitats Directive site.

abstracts.Om het model voor de fluctuatie van de g: To generate the groundwater-table fluctuation model, field measurements are carried out in spring and autumn to measure groundwater-table depth. Measurements are made in a temporary borehole after the groundwater level in the hole has stabilised. This point dataset contains location, date and depth in centimetres below ground level. The groundwater-table depth model is part of the Key Registry of the Subsurface (BRO). It consists of several groundwater characteristics that together represent long-term average fluctuations in groundwater-table depth: mean highest groundwater level (GHG), mean lowest groundwater level (GLG), and the groundwater class (Gt) derived from them. Until recently, the groundwater class formed part of another registration object, the Soil Map of the Netherlands at scale 1:50,000. For ecological and other applications, mean spring groundwater level (GVG) has also been added to the model.

abstracts.Wetlands zijn de natte natuurgebieden in: Wetlands are the wet nature areas of the Netherlands. The Convention on Wetlands was signed in Ramsar, Iran, on 2 February 1971. The Netherlands was one of the sixteen countries that signed the Convention at that time and ratified it in 1980. The Ramsar Convention is one of the oldest international nature-conservation treaties. By August 2004, 138 countries had signed the Wetlands Convention. Its purpose is to protect wetlands and their associated plant and animal species. Under the Ramsar Convention, wetlands are officially defined as areas of marsh, fen, peatland or water, whether natural or artificial, permanent or temporary, with water that is static or flowing, fresh, brackish or salt, including areas of marine water whose depth at low tide does not exceed six metres. This also includes riparian and coastal zones adjacent to wetlands and islands or bodies of marine water lying within them. The Netherlands has 44 Wetlands in total. These Wetlands have been placed by the Ramsar Secretariat on the Ramsar List of Wetlands of International Importance. Wetlands International maintains an extensive database for every listed site; this database and other information about the Ramsar Convention are available through the Ramsar Secretariat. Between 1980 and 1995, the Netherlands placed eighteen Wetlands on the Ramsar List, followed by another 26 in 2000. Countries joining the Wetlands Convention primarily assume a moral obligation to implement the Ramsar Convention. Its provisions are less prescriptive and binding than obligations under European law arising from the Birds Directive and Habitats Directive. Areas selected under those directives are known as Natura 2000 sites. In the Netherlands, all Wetlands except one are also Birds Directive areas and therefore Natura 2000 sites. The role and potential of wetlands are often underestimated. They have important ecological functions, for example as indispensable locations on international bird migration routes and as nursery areas for fish and marine animals. People also benefit from wetlands, especially in the densely populated Dutch delta. They are used for fisheries, recreation and tourism, navigation, water storage for flood protection, drinking-water supply and as attractive living environments. Careful management and use of these opportunities are therefore important. In total, almost one million hectares of the Netherlands are Wetland, representing 27% of the country's total area including territorial waters.

service_abstracts.\"Deze dataset bevat gegevens van Nederl: This dataset contains data on groundwater use in the Netherlands from the Key Registry of the Subsurface (BRO). It concerns data on groundwater-use systems that are subject to notification or permit requirements, and the quantities of groundwater periodically reported to the competent authority as abstracted and returned by those systems. These aggregated data have been harmonised to the INSPIRE theme Environmental Monitoring Facilities. A groundwater-use system is a subsurface construction that uses groundwater directly or indirectly. Direct use includes groundwater abstraction or infiltration of water into the subsurface. Indirect use makes use of the heat capacity of groundwater, as in a ground-source energy system.

service_abstracts.Deze dataset bevat de gegevens van neder: This dataset contains data on groundwater monitoring in the Netherlands from the Key Registry of the Subsurface (BRO). It contains the principal characteristics of groundwater monitoring wells and the associated groundwater monitoring networks for which those wells have been used, together with characteristics of groundwater-level and groundwater-composition observations made in those wells. Groundwater monitoring means observing the condition of groundwater in a given area, or more precisely in a particular part of the subsurface, over an extended period. The size of the area and monitoring depth vary by groundwater monitoring network. Monitoring concerns groundwater level (quantity) and/or groundwater composition (quality), for which periodic measurements are carried out. A description of this dataset is available in the BRO Product Environment.

service_abstracts.Dit bestand geeft de grenzen van de Nati: This dataset shows the boundaries of the National Parks as specified by the Park Secretariats between August 2005 and November 2005, with updates in January 2007 and August 2007. A correction to the boundary of Drents-Friese Wold National Park is still pending. The dataset contains 21 National Parks in total: 18 parks designated by the Minister of Agriculture, Nature and Food Quality (one of them still being established), two private parks and one cross-border park designated by the Benelux Committee of Ministers. The GIS dataset also contains 'development areas'. These are areas intended, preferably, to become part of a National Park in the future but which have not yet been designated. They are therefore NOT part of the relevant park and have no formal status. Boundaries in the GIS dataset may differ from those in the Management and Development Plan (BIP). Each National Park has a BIP submitted to the Minister for approval, and each BIP includes a map of the park boundary. That boundary is a snapshot in time. Park boundaries may change slightly over time through small land acquisitions or exchanges; such changes are incorporated during periodic BIP updates. A BIP may therefore lag behind, or be ahead of, the boundaries in this dataset.

service_abstracts.Een milieuhygiënisch bodemonderzoek is e: An environmental soil investigation is an investigation in which the presence of contaminants in the soil within the investigation site is assessed. It determines the nature of any contamination (which substances occur at concentrations above the natural background level) and its degree (how measured concentrations compare with permitted levels under a national or local standards framework). The soil investigation is generally carried out by third parties, for example under contract to a data owner that is also the project initiator. It may also be submitted by a project initiator other than a government body to the competent authority as part of a statutory procedure, such as a permit procedure or notification. The result of the environmental soil investigation includes information on measurement points (including boreholes and monitoring wells), sampling, field observations and laboratory analyses of field samples (soil and groundwater), and the soil investigation report. So-called historical investigations, based only on archive research, and investigations evaluating completed remediation or excavation works (verification investigations as part of environmental supervision) are also part of this registration object. Statutory standards and protocols (NEN and SIKB) based on the Soil Quality Regulation 2022 apply to environmental soil investigations. In many cases, staff performing the work operate under certification.

service_abstracts.Gegevens van geotechnisch sondeeronderzo: Characteristic-set data from geotechnical cone penetration tests as stored in the Key Registry of the Subsurface (BRO). A geotechnical cone penetration test (CPT) is an investigation intended to obtain information about the soil or geological structure of the subsurface by pushing a cone-shaped probe into the ground and taking in-situ measurements. Traditionally, the probe is used to determine cone resistance and friction during penetration, from which mechanical properties of the subsurface can be derived. Over time, probes have evolved to support a broad range of measurements. For more information, see www.basisregistratieondergrond.nl.

service_abstracts.Inspire geharmoniseerde dataset van het: INSPIRE-harmonised national Water Framework Directive (WFD) Groundwater Bodies dataset. Under the WFD, a groundwater body is an important unit about which water managers must report. A groundwater body is a coherent mass of groundwater. The Dutch Water Act uses a broader interpretation of the term than, for example, the WFD or the Groundwater Directive. The European directives limit the definition to water below the ground surface in the saturated zone, i.e. all water below the groundwater table. Dutch legislation does not make this distinction: under the Water Act, all water moving freely in the soil is groundwater. The 2009 Water Quality Requirements and Monitoring Decree (Bkmw 2009) does, however, contain the narrower European definition, under which only water in the saturated zone is groundwater. The groundwater objectives of the WFD and Groundwater Directive therefore focus on that water. All groundwater in the Netherlands belongs to a groundwater body. The Netherlands distinguishes 23 groundwater bodies, which are designated and managed by the provinces.

service_abstracts.Web Coverage Service (WCS) van het Actue: Web Coverage Service (WCS) for the Current Elevation Model of the Netherlands (AHN). AHN is the digital elevation map for the whole of the Netherlands and contains detailed, precise elevation data with at least 10 height measurements per square metre. AHN is a collaboration between the provinces, national government and water authorities. Elevation is measured using airborne laser altimetry, in which an aircraft scans the Earth's surface with a laser beam. The current AHN is version 4, acquired during 2020, 2021 and 2022. For more information, see https://ahn.nl. This WCS contains AHN raster datasets at 0.5 m resolution, distinguishing between the Digital Terrain Model (DTM) and Digital Surface Model (DSM). The DTM is intended to represent bare ground: all points classified as 'ground' are resampled to a raster using a squared inverse-distance weighting method. The DSM is intended as a raw surface model: all points except those classified as 'water' are resampled to a raster using the same squared IDW method.

service_abstracts.Wetlands zijn de natte natuurgebieden in: Wetlands are the wet nature areas of the Netherlands. The Convention on Wetlands was signed in Ramsar, Iran, on 2 February 1971. The Netherlands was one of the sixteen countries that signed the Convention at that time and ratified it in 1980. The Ramsar Convention is one of the oldest international nature-conservation treaties. By August 2004, 138 countries had signed the Wetlands Convention. Its purpose is to protect wetlands and their associated plant and animal species. Under the Ramsar Convention, wetlands are officially defined as areas of marsh, fen, peatland or water, whether natural or artificial, permanent or temporary, with water that is static or flowing, fresh, brackish or salt, including areas of marine water whose depth at low tide does not exceed six metres. This also includes riparian and coastal zones adjacent to wetlands and islands or bodies of marine water lying within them. The Netherlands has 44 Wetlands in total. These Wetlands have been placed by the Ramsar Secretariat on the Ramsar List of Wetlands of International Importance. Wetlands International maintains an extensive database for every listed site; this database and other information about the Ramsar Convention are available through the Ramsar Secretariat. Between 1980 and 1995, the Netherlands placed eighteen Wetlands on the Ramsar List, followed by another 26 in 2000. Countries joining the Wetlands Convention primarily assume a moral obligation to implement the Ramsar Convention. Its provisions are less prescriptive and binding than obligations under European law arising from the Birds Directive and Habitats Directive. Areas selected under those directives are known as Natura 2000 sites. In the Netherlands, all Wetlands except one are also Birds Directive areas and therefore Natura 2000 sites. The role and potential of wetlands are often underestimated. They have important ecological functions, for example as indispensable locations on international bird migration routes and as nursery areas for fish and marine animals. People also benefit from wetlands, especially in the densely populated Dutch delta. They are used for fisheries, recreation and tourism, navigation, water storage for flood protection, drinking-water supply and as attractive living environments. Careful management and use of these opportunities are therefore important. In total, almost one million hectares of the Netherlands are Wetland, representing 27% of the country's total area including territorial waters.
